facts.fact: The GPE KIX blog states that the PIN-driven EMIS, launched nationally in March 2024, now covers all 976 primary and secondary schools (976 of 976), with individual-level tracking of students and staff; the source counts schools covered, not schools entering data, and elsewhere says the EMIS currently provides aggregate enrolment numbers; the present-tense figure is undated, so the document's published date is used.
The blog states that the PIN-driven EMIS covers all 976 primary and secondary schools since its national launch in March 2024; undated in the present tense, so the document's published date is used.

The blog calls the system the ministry's own, designed and scaled by the Ministry of Education and Training with help from UNICEF and civil society, and reports the ministry's departments presenting their uses of it at the February 2025 exchange.
The blog refers to Eswatini's SEMIS as a pilot and to its roll-out as still to come, with no number of pilot schools; undated, so the document's published date is used.

systems.tiers: all 976 primary and secondary schools; ministry departments

systems.system: PIN validation against Home Affairs records
systems.owner: Ministry of Education and Training; Home Affairs
systems.tiers: schools submit paper claim forms with each learner's PIN, checked at regional offices; to be automated with SEMIS

note: The document pulls two ways and the parent must weigh it: it describes the EMIS as PIN-driven with individual-level student tracking in all 976 schools, and also says the EMIS gives aggregate enrolment numbers while per-learner PINs still travel on paper claim forms until SEMIS is rolled out. The first is classed emis on the document's own description; it does not say schools enter attendance or results, so no kept fact is taken. The 976 is primary and secondary together, with no primary figure.
